Moraga.headline: The storm has one more round of rough weather before a chilly East Bay weekend
Moraga.text: The storm isn't quite finished with Moraga. Another round of downpours is possible Thursday as the system's colder center swings through, and a few showers could bring thunder or small hail. Rain should gradually ease later Thursday, though a passing shower may linger into Friday morning. Then the feel of the weather changes: colder air moves in, bringing crisp, chilly starts Friday and Saturday. Keep an eye on the weekend, too—a weaker weather system could deliver a few more showers, but it looks far less impressive than this week's storm. Monday may bring a welcome pause. Forecast models are already hinting at another potentially wetter system around Tuesday, giving the unsettled pattern one more chapter.

Lafayette.headline: More showers could rumble through Thursday before a colder, quieter weekend
Lafayette.text: Reliez Valley may have one more soggy chapter before this storm finally moves on. The system's colder center is expected to cross Thursday, bringing another chance for heavy showers, with an isolated rumble of thunder or small hail possible. The steadiest rain should become more scattered later in the day, although a few showers could hang on into Friday morning. Colder air follows, setting up some distinctly chilly starts to the weekend. Saturday's next weather system looks weaker, but it could still sprinkle the valley with occasional showers into Sunday. Monday is shaping up as the best chance for a breather. Beyond that, forecast models are increasingly signaling another potentially wetter system around Tuesday—one we'll be watching closely as its track comes into focus.

Danville.headline: Thursday could bring a final burst of heavy showers, then a welcome break
Danville.text: Don't be fooled if the rain lets up for a while—Thursday could deliver another burst of wet weather to Sycamore Valley. The storm's colder center is expected to pass through the region, creating another opportunity for heavy showers and perhaps an isolated thunderstorm or small hail. The downpours should become more scattered by Thursday afternoon, with a few lingering showers possible early Friday. Colder air then settles in, making Friday and Saturday mornings feel more like winter. A weaker system could bring a few showers back over the weekend, but it should be a much quieter affair than this week's storm. Monday looks calmer, while forecast models are beginning to tease another potentially wetter system around Tuesday. There's more to watch, but plenty of time for that forecast to change.

Greenbrook.headline: One more round of rain may arrive Thursday before the weekend turns colder
Greenbrook.text: Greenbrook isn't quite in the clear yet. As the storm's colder center moves across the Bay Area Thursday, another round of heavy showers could sweep through, with a slight chance of thunder or small hail. The strongest bursts should gradually fade during the afternoon, but don't be surprised by a lingering shower into early Friday. Behind the storm, colder air takes over and brings a chilly start to the weekend. Another, weaker weather system may brush the area Saturday and Sunday with a few additional showers, though it looks modest compared with the storm now departing. Monday could offer a quieter window before attention turns to Tuesday. Forecast models are hinting at another potentially wetter system then, but its timing and strength are still taking shape.
